입다.x: It's cold today, so I wore a coat.
입다.t: 입다 is for clothes worn on the body; shoes/socks use 신다, hats/glasses use 쓰다. Regular verb (not ㅂ irregular).

아름답다.t: 아름답다 sounds more elegant than 예쁘다 — often used for scenery, music or a person's heart.

똑바로.ex: 이 길로 똑바로 가면 학교가 있어요.
똑바로.x: If you go straight along this road, you'll find the school.

역시.forms: 역시 + sentence; 역시! = I knew it!
역시.ex: 역시 엄마가 만든 김치가 제일 맛있어요.
역시.x: As expected, the kimchi Mom makes is the best.
역시.t: 역시! on its own means 'I knew it!' when something meets expectations.

쉽게.forms: 쉽게 + verb; from 쉽다 (ㅂ irregular: 쉬워요)
쉽게.ex: 이 책은 아이들도 쉽게 읽을 수 있어요.
쉽게.x: Even kids can read this book easily.
쉽게.e: From 쉽다 'to be easy' + -게, the usual way to make an adverb.

증가하다.ex: 혼자 사는 사람이 계속 증가하고 있습니다.
증가하다.x: The number of people living alone keeps increasing.
증가하다.t: Formal, common in news and reports; in conversation 늘어나다 sounds more natural.

동기.m: classmate (same year), peer who started at the same time
동기.x: I still often meet my college classmates.
동기.e: Literally 'same period' — people who entered school or a company together.
동기.t: Homonym warning: 동기 (動機) also means 'motive'.

동기.x: The police are investigating the motive for the crime.
동기.t: Its homonym 동기 means 'peer from the same year or class'.

손바닥.x: I was nervous, so my palms got sweaty.
손바닥.e: 손 'hand' + 바닥 'bottom, floor'; compare 발바닥 'sole of the foot'.

곡.ex: 이 곡은 제가 제일 좋아하는 노래예요.
곡.t: Use 곡 to count songs: 노래 한 곡 부를게요, 'I'll sing one song'.

어리석다.ex: 그런 어리석은 실수를 다시는 하지 않을 거예요.
어리석다.x: I'll never make such a foolish mistake again.
어리석다.e: Middle Korean 어리다 meant 'foolish' before it shifted to mean 'young'.

잡수시다.x: Grandpa, have you had your meal?
잡수시다.e: 잡수다 (itself an honorific of 먹다) + honorific -시-; the contracted 잡숫다 is also standard.
잡수시다.t: Pronounced [잡쑤시다]: the final ㅂ makes the next ㅅ tense. Use it for grandparents and the elderly; more deferential than 드시다.

정화.ex: 나무와 식물은 공기를 정화하는 역할을 해요.
정화.x: Trees and plants help purify the air.

강화.x: The police stepped up their crackdown on drunk driving.

등본.m: certified copy (of a register), resident registration copy
등본.x: I got a copy of my resident registration from the community center.
등본.e: Literally 'a copied-out version of the original' record.
등본.t: Koreans say 등본을 떼다 for getting one issued, literally 'to tear off' a copy.

통째로.forms: 통째로 + verb: 통째로 먹다, 통째로 외우다
통째로.ex: 그는 책 한 권을 통째로 외웠어요.
통째로.e: 통 'whole lump' + -째 'as it is', as in 껍질째 'peel and all'.

병환.x: My grandmother was hospitalized due to illness.
병환.t: Honorific of 병, used for the illness of grandparents, parents or other elders, never your own. Often with 편찮으시다.

양반.m: yangban, the Joseon aristocracy; (casual) a gentleman, this guy
양반.ex: 조선 시대 양반은 주로 공부를 하며 과거를 준비했어요.
양반.x: In the Joseon era, yangban mostly studied and prepared for the civil service exam.
양반.e: Literally 'the two ranks': the civil and military officials who lined up at court.
양반.t: In casual speech 양반 can mean 'a decent man' or just 'this guy': 이 양반이 정말!

증대하다.m: to increase, to enlarge, to boost
증대하다.ex: 이번 정책은 수출을 크게 증대할 것으로 기대됩니다.
증대하다.x: This policy is expected to greatly increase exports.

무르익다.m: to ripen fully; to mature, to reach its peak
무르익다.x: As autumn reached its peak, the mountains turned red with fall foliage.
무르익다.e: Built from 무르다 'to be soft' plus 익다 'to ripen' — fruit soft and ripe.
무르익다.t: Pronounced [무르익따]. Often figurative: 분위기가 무르익다 'the mood warms up.'

입안하다.m: to draft, to draw up (a plan, policy, or bill)
입안하다.ex: 정부는 새로운 교통 정책을 입안하고 있습니다.
입안하다.x: The government is drafting a new transportation policy.
입안하다.e: Literally 'set up a plan' — drafting a policy or bill.
입안하다.t: Don't confuse it with native 입안 'inside the mouth' (입 + 안).

진보적.ex: 그 정치인은 교육 문제에 진보적인 입장을 보였습니다.
진보적.x: That politician took a progressive stance on education.

인과응보.m: you reap what you sow; karma
인과응보.ex: 남을 속인 그가 벌을 받은 것은 인과응보예요.
인과응보.x: It's karma that he got punished after deceiving others.
인과응보.e: Literally 'cause and effect, answered in kind' — a Buddhist idea.

수출입.ex: 올해 수출입 규모가 역대 최고를 기록했습니다.
수출입.x: This year, the volume of exports and imports hit an all-time high.
수출입.t: Pronounced [수추립]: the ㄹ carries over to 입.

빙산.ex: 지구가 따뜻해지면서 빙산이 빠르게 녹고 있어요.
빙산.x: As the earth gets warmer, icebergs are melting quickly.
빙산.t: 빙산의 일각 'the tip of the iceberg' is a very common idiom.

양수.m: acquisition by transfer, taking over (rights or property)
양수.ex: 그 회사는 경쟁사의 사업 부문을 양수했습니다.
양수.x: The company acquired a business division from its competitor.
양수.e: Literally 'receive what's handed over'; homonyms mean 'positive number' and 'amniotic fluid'.
양수.t: Pairs with 양도: the 양도인 hands over, the 양수인 receives, as in a 양도양수 계약.

국민참여재판.x: The defendant can request a citizen participation trial.
국민참여재판.e: Literally 'trial with the people taking part'; introduced in Korea in 2008.

병원균.ex: 손을 자주 씻으면 병원균의 전파를 막을 수 있어요.
병원균.x: Washing your hands often can stop the spread of germs.

분자식.ex: 우리가 매일 마시는 물의 분자식은 H₂O입니다.
분자식.x: The molecular formula of the water we drink every day is H2O.

혼비백산.m: being scared out of one's wits
혼비백산.ex: 골목에서 갑자기 큰 개가 짖어서 혼비백산했어요.
혼비백산.x: A big dog suddenly barked in the alley, and I was scared out of my wits.
혼비백산.e: Literally 'the soul flies off, the spirit scatters'.
혼비백산.t: Common as 혼비백산하다, or 혼비백산하여 달아나다 'to flee in terror'.

상쇄하다.x: Rising exports offset weak domestic demand.
상쇄하다.e: Literally 'mutually cancel' — two forces wiping each other out.
상쇄하다.t: The second syllable is read 쇄, not 살 — a classic reading trap for this hanja.

영위하다.m: to lead (a life), to run, to carry on (a business or activity)
영위하다.ex: 누구나 인간다운 삶을 영위할 권리가 있습니다.
영위하다.x: Everyone has the right to lead a decent human life.
영위하다.t: Most common object: 삶 or 생활 — 삶을 영위하다 = to lead a life.

속되다.ex: 속된 말로 하면 그 사람은 금수저예요.
속되다.x: To put it in slang, he was born with a silver spoon.
속되다.t: 속된 말로 'to put it crudely' is a common way to introduce slang. Pronounced [속뙤다].

혹자.ex: 혹자는 그 계획이 실패할 거라고 말합니다.
혹자.x: Some say that plan will fail.
혹자.e: Literally 'some person'; -자 = person, as in 과학자, 운전자.
혹자.t: Formal, mostly in writing as 혹자는 ~라고 한다 'some say …'.

가부장제.ex: 가부장제의 영향은 아직도 명절 문화에 남아 있어요.
가부장제.x: The influence of patriarchy still remains in holiday customs.

경기순환.x: Booms and recessions repeat according to the business cycle.
경기순환.e: Literally 'the economy going around in cycles.'
